primitives.name: Referee Decision Finality
primitives.verbatim_quote: The decision of the Referee upon all matters not specifically designated under the duties of other officials shall be final.
primitives.assumptions: Decision space is partitioned into referee-exclusive and shared jurisdictions; referee's authority is absolute in non-shared domains.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When referee's jurisdiction overlaps with umpire's, precedence is enforced.

layer2.mapping: Referee decision-making mirrors Bayesian posterior update over rule-space, with finality as prior override in non-designated domains.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of referee overrides vs. umpire penalties.

primitives.name: Referee Penalty Precedence
primitives.verbatim_quote: In making his decisions the Referee must recognize and allow precedence to any penalty declared by the Umpire.
primitives.assumptions: Umpire's penalty declaration is a stochastic variable with higher information content than referee's local observation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When referee observes conflicting evidence, umpire's penalty is treated as a likelihood-weighted signal.

layer2.mapping: Penalty precedence is modeled as a likelihood ratio test between referee and umpire observations, with umpire's verdict as a sufficient statistic.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of referee decisions overturned by umpire penalty declarations.

primitives.name: Referee Appeal Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: The Referee may appeal to either of the other officials for testimony upon points within his jurisdiction.
primitives.assumptions: Appeal is a structured communication protocol enabling cross-official consensus-building.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When referee lacks sufficient data, appeal enables information fusion across official roles.

layer2.mapping: Appeal mechanism mirrors belief propagation in graphical models, where referee acts as node seeking evidence from neighbors.
layer2.telemetry: Number of appeals per game and resolution rate.

primitives.name: Referee Reporting Obligation
primitives.verbatim_quote: He must report to the Umpire any infringement of certain indicated sections of Rule XVII., Rule XXIII., and Rule XXIV., as well as all cases of holding or unlawful use of hands or arms which come under his observation.
primitives.assumptions: Reporting is a deterministic function of observed rule violation types and their categorization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violation classification triggers reporting iff rule section matches specified set.

layer2.mapping: Reporting obligation is a conditional probability model P(report|violation_type), with rule sections as categorical predictors.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of reported violations against observed infractions.

reasoning_traces.think:
The referee’s authority is defined through a layered decision structure: finality in non-overlapping domains, precedence in overlapping ones, and appeal for missing data. This forms a hierarchical Bayesian network where the referee acts as a top-level decision node, with the umpire and other officials as evidence-generating nodes. The system exhibits duality between local observation and global coordination, where local decisions are subject to global correction via penalty precedence. The appeal mechanism introduces a form of belief propagation, allowing the referee to resolve uncertainty through cross-official consensus. Reporting obligations ensure that rule violations are transmitted to the umpire, creating a feedback loop that maintains consistency across rule interpretations. Failure modes include misalignment of jurisdiction, delayed or absent appeals, and incomplete reporting, all of which can lead to inconsistent rule enforcement. The system is robust under normal conditions but vulnerable to adversarial behavior or miscommunication among officials.
